# MainWP answers recorded on the bench

Each file is one answer of MainWP Dashboard 6.4.1's REST API (version 2): `what` was asked, the HTTP `status` and the `body`, recorded on 9 November 2026 against a throwaway dashboard and WordPress site in containers. No request header is kept, so no key. Re-record from a clean throwaway dashboard and adjust the ids and times the tests expect.

`key-over-http.json` is MainWP answering a key sent over plain HTTP from another host: it was accepted, because the dashboard's own address is HTTPS. The module therefore refuses an http:// dashboard address itself.

The answers of the bench's sixth run (10 November 2026, run `R-20261110T122346`) show a broken connection and what mends it: a site whose MainWP Child was switched off (`site-sync-child-off`, `site-get-disconnected`, `sites-list-disconnected`, `site-reconnect-child-off`) and switched on again (`site-sync-child-back`, `site-get-child-back`, `site-reconnect-connected`); a Child whose connection data was cleared (`site-sync-keys-lost`, `site-get-keys-lost`, `site-reconnect-rekeyed`); a site whose connecting administrator was deleted (`site-sync-admin-gone`, `site-get-admin-gone`, `site-reconnect-admin-gone`, `sites-add-while-dead`), pointed at another administrator (`site-edit-admin`, `site-reconnect-after-edit`, `site-sync-after-edit`, `site-get-after-edit`), or removed and added again (`site-remove-dead`, `sites-add-after-dead-remove`, `sites-add-after-reactivate`, `sites-add-after-reinstall`, `sites-add-after-child-disconnect`); a site suspended while disconnected (`site-get-suspended-disconnected`); and a site flagged as staging in the dashboard's database (`site-get-staging`, `sites-list-staging`, `site-remove-staging`, `sites-add-after-staging-remove`). `site-get-staging.json` replaces a file that had been made by hand: the recorded row is shorter than an ordinary one and carries no `is_staging` field at all.

The answers of the bench's eighth run (11 November 2026, run `C-20261111T152142`, MainWP Dashboard 6.4.2.1) show MainWP's users routes: a site's administrators listed (`users-list-admins`, `users-list-admins-host-route`), refused for a disconnected site (`users-list-disconnected`) and for no site named (`users-list-no-site`); the care account made (`users-create-care`) and made again with the same login after it was deleted (`users-create-care-again`); and the refusals of `users/create` (`users-create-refused-login-exists`, `users-create-refused-email-exists`, `users-create-refused-disconnected`, `users-create-refused-unknown-site`, `users-create-refused-form`); the dashboard pointed at the care account and synced (`site-edit-admin-care`, `site-sync-as-care`); the care account deleted on the site (`site-sync-care-gone`, `site-get-care-gone`) and the sync once it was made again (`site-sync-care-remade`); and a site the host prepared, added as its care account (`sites-add-as-care-host-route`). MainWP repeats the password it was sent in `data.user_info.user_pass`; the bench replaced it with `[removed: N characters]` before keeping the answer, and the tests put a password back where they need to show that it reaches no message. The bench's `seconds` field is left out here, as in the files above.
